DiT-XL/2 at 256 px on 8x H100 (DDP, 32 images per GPU, global batch 256): the reference train.py (fp32 + TF32, VAE encode every step in fp32, per-parameter EMA loop, foreach AdamW) runs 0.3005 s/update; bf16 autocast + pre-computed latents + torch.compile + fused AdamW + foreach EMA runs 0.09724 s (x3.09). One change at a time from bf16 + latents (0.1459 s): compile x1.31, fused AdamW x1.08, foreach EMA x1.03 (EMA off x1.04), gradient_as_bucket_view x1.03 (-2.5 GiB); DDP static_graph x0.996 and 100 MB buckets x1.002 are within noise; timm's unfused attention costs x0.86, cuDNN-first SDPA x1.011. TF32 matters in fp32 only: TF32 off is x0.32.

Online VAE encoding is a fixed cost per image, whatever the DiT size: at 256 px with 32 images per GPU on 8x H100 the bf16 step minus the same step with cached latents is 0.074 s (S/2), 0.074 s (B/2), 0.073 s (L/2), 0.077 s (XL/2) and 0.317 s at 512 px (XL/2). Caching latents is therefore worth x3.57 (S/2, 33M), x2.76 (B/2, 130M), x1.68 (L/2, 458M), x1.53 (XL/2, 675M), x1.69 at 512 px. The encode runs on the GPU inside the step: 1, 2, 8 or 16 loader workers instead of 4 move XL/2 by x1.001, x0.985, x0.997, x1.017; a bf16 instead of fp32 VAE gives x1.14.

DiT size changes what pays (256 px, 32 images per GPU, 8x H100): bf16 autocast with the VAE encode in the step gives x1.03 (S/2), x1.16 (B/2), x1.27 (L/2), x1.35 (XL/2) - small models are bound by the encode and data path, not by matmuls; the whole stack (bf16 + latents + compile + fused AdamW + foreach EMA) gives x4.76 (S/2), x4.45 (B/2), x3.27 (L/2), x3.09 (XL/2). With the stack the small models leave the GPUs partly idle: SM utilisation 61 % (S/2), 73 % (B/2), 92 % (L/2), 84 % (XL/2).

DiT-XL/2 256 px, bf16 + cached latents on 8x H100: samples/s per GPU at 16 / 32 / 64 / 128 images per GPU = 158 / 219 / 277 / 311 (nvidia-smi peak 25.8 GiB / 33.7 GiB / 45.9 GiB / 69.4 GiB); a larger per-GPU batch also changes the global batch, so that is a workload decision. At a fixed global batch the larger micro-batch wins: 32 x 1 vs 16 x 2 accumulation x1.17, 64 x 1 vs 32 x 2 x1.12; an all-reduce on every micro-batch instead of no_sync costs x0.94.

DiT-XL/2 at 512 px (1024 tokens) on 8x H100, 32 images per GPU: fp32 + TF32 runs out of memory (D500, 79.1 GiB); bf16 with the VAE encode in the step 0.7786 s (69.0 GiB), + cached latents 0.4615 s (x1.69), + compile + fused AdamW + foreach EMA 0.335 s (x2.32, 58.8 GiB).

SD1.5 UNet full fine-tune (diffusers train_text_to_image.py, 512 px, 16 images per GPU, 8x H100): keep bf16 (fp32 is x0.39, fp32 + TF32 x0.49, fp16 x0.983); torch.compile through accelerate's dynamo config gives x1.18 and cuDNN-first SDPA x1.05, while xformers (x1.002), TF32 in bf16 (x1.001), cudnn.benchmark (x0.998) and 8 loader workers (x1.001) are within noise. Costs: gradient checkpointing x0.87, 8-bit Adam x0.95, EMA x0.96 (per-parameter loop) / x0.97 (foreach) / x0.54 (EMA copy on the CPU), 0 loader workers x0.54. The step is not compute-bound (SM utilisation 82 %); the small synthetic set adds a DataLoader stall at every epoch boundary (window mean / median 1.13) that the median step time leaves out.

SDXL UNet full fine-tune (diffusers train_text_to_image_sdxl.py, 1024 px, latents and text embeddings pre-computed by the script, 8x H100): with gradient checkpointing and 4 images per GPU a step takes 0.5844 s (61.4 GiB); without checkpointing x1.20 but 79.2 GiB of 80 GB (2 per GPU: 64.4 GiB); torch.compile x1.24; cuDNN-first SDPA x1.011; xformers is slower (x0.94), so are EMA (x0.94) and 8-bit Adam (x0.92, -22.6 GiB). At a fixed global batch 4 x 1 beats 2 x 2 accumulation by x1.38.

No backend wins on every model: measure it per model.

Pre-computed latents and text embeddings are worth little for 6-20B transformers at 1024 px on 8x H100: FLUX.1 LoRA latents x1.04, prompt embeddings x1.03, both x1.08 (one instance prompt on both sides); Qwen-Image LoRA latents x1.06; Z-Image LoRA latents x1.05; FLUX.1 full with per-image captions encoded every step vs one instance prompt encoded once x1.014 (a workload comparison). They still free the encoders' memory (-4.7 GiB for FLUX.1 LoRA). For sub-1B DiTs the VAE encode dominates: latents x3.57 (DiT-S/2) to x1.53 (DiT-XL/2).

FP8 did not pay for LoRA training at batch 1 per GPU on 8x H100: torchao float8 training of Z-Image (diffusers --do_fp8_training) runs x0.45 with and x0.44 without gradient checkpointing; float8 storage of Qwen-Image's frozen DiT (DiffSynth --fp8_models) runs x0.67 for -19.1 GiB of memory. Full training of DiT-XL/2 (bf16 + cached latents) with torchao float8 Linear layers: x0.43 without and x0.89 with torch.compile; float8 on top of the whole DiT stack (cached latents, compile, fused AdamW, foreach EMA): XL/2 256 px x0.89, S/2 x0.93, XL/2 512 px x0.96.

EMA of the trained weights is one more pass over all parameters per update (8x H100): SD1.5 UNet x0.96 with diffusers' per-parameter loop, x0.97 with foreach ops, x0.54 with the EMA copy on the CPU (--offload_ema; avoid it when the GPU has room); SDXL x0.94; DiT-XL/2: dropping the loop EMA x1.04, foreach instead of the loop x1.03.

At a fixed global batch, the largest micro-batch that fits beats gradient accumulation (8x H100): DiT-XL/2 32 x 1 vs 16 x 2 x1.17; SD1.5 16 x 1 vs 8 x 2 x1.13, 32 x 1 vs 16 x 2 x1.08; SDXL 4 x 1 vs 2 x 2 x1.38; FLUX.1 LoRA 4 x 1 vs 1 x 4 x1.13 and vs 2 x 2 x1.04.

Optimizer on 8x H100: torch fused AdamW gives x1.08 on DiT-XL/2; bitsandbytes 8-bit Adam is slower for UNet full fine-tunes (SD1.5 x0.95, SDXL x0.92 at 4 per GPU, x0.95 at 8) and saves optimizer memory (SDXL -22.6 GiB).

diffusers vs DiffSynth-Studio on the same LoRA r32 workload (1024 px, batch 1 per GPU, 8x H100), each at its reference settings: FLUX.1-dev 0.9358 s vs 1.074 s, Qwen-Image 0.9059 s vs 1.102 s, Z-Image 0.7089 s vs 0.8148 s (s/update).
